title: Allowance and Responsibility: First Lessons in Self-Management
summary: At this age, the child becomes ready to learn responsibility through simple tasks and a small allowance. Giving him age-appropriate household responsibilities (tidying his bed, helping with the table) builds his competence and confidence—do not burden him beyond his capacity. A small, regular allowance teaches him the value of money, saving, and choice. Do not tie basic tasks to money (cooperation is a family duty), but reward initiative. Allow him to face small natural consequences (forgetting his duty = bearing the result) so he may learn. A child who is given gradual responsibility develops independence and discipline that will serve him in his studies and life.
try_this: This week: Assign your child one consistent household responsibility that suits his age, and let him carry it out without constant reminders. Observe its impact on his sense of competence.
reflection_prompts: What responsibility appropriate for his age can you entrust to your child to build his confidence?
How do you balance between helping him and letting him face small consequences from which he can learn?
